Q: Can I force GCC and Clang to reject `__typeof__` in C standard mode? A:

typeof is gcc an extension.

from gcc documentation:

If you are writing a header file that must work when included in ISO C programs, write __typeof__ instead of typeof. See Alternate Keywords.

How can I make those compilers to reject typeof?

When compiled for gcc you should poison the __typeof__

#ifdef __GNUC__
#pragma GCC poison __typeof__
#endif

int main(void)
{
    int a;
    __typeof__(a) b;
    return 0;
}

https://godbolt.org/z/5T6es19E8

More detailed explanation:

__typeof__ is not ISO C17, but it is in the implementation-reserved namespace. In C, identifiers beginning with _ followed by another _ are reserved for the implementation, and the C standard says such identifiers are reserved “for any use”.

GCC documents exactly this behaviour: -std=c17 disables GNU extension keywords such as plain typeof, but GCC provides the double-underscore spelling as an “alternate keyword”. GCC also explicitly says that -Wpedantic does not warn for alternate keywords whose names begin and end with __

Q: Is there any way to get a list of members only videos? A:

Via API, I don't think there is a way (yet).

But you can use external tools to scrape this information.

For example, using yt-dlp:

yt-dlp {channel_URL} --flat-playlist --print title,url --cookies-from-browser chrome

(You can include your cookies/credentials in other ways, of course.)

Q: DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN on Google App Engine website A:

In my case, I deployed my app in AWS Amplify and got my domain from GoDaddy. When this error was coming and my site was crashing, all I did was waited for 48 hours for the nameservers to transfer from GoDaddy to AWS. The process is called 'propagation time' and yes, its silly because who wants to wait for 48 hours in a world where nobody has patience.

GoDaddy is slow. if you dont want to deal with this problem, then I would suggest to get your domain from AWS route 53 only, instead of buying them from other third party companies like GoDaddy.
